title.narrative: Kunzila Integrated Landscape Management and WASH Project

description.narrative: Kunzila Integrated Landscape Management & WASH (KILMWA) is a Five Year (2020-2024) Project that has set out an innovative and comprehensive vision to contribute to a more prosperous and healthy population in Kunzila watershed Participatory Integrated Watershed Management and WASH interventions in alignment with existing initiatives and programmes in the area. The project is funded by The Royal Netherlands Embassy in Ethiopia. The project is implemented by WLRC in partnership with SNV. The project brings together the unique combination of experience and expertise, networks and alliances, and proven approaches the WLRC and SNV have in PIWM and WASH sectors, respectively in Ethiopia, region and globe.

description.narrative: A total budget of € 121890 was allocated to finance development activities planned under Outcome8: Efficient and responsive project management, facilitation of timely implementation, and functional MEL. The utilization was 47.8% of the planned budget. The reasons are some of the joint management activities, PSC meetings at woreda and regional levels, were not implemented due to political instability, election, etc. and more attention was given to kick start the project at the site level, and some required materials for KWT/CWF were not procured as their office was not finalized.

A total budget of € 175996 was allocated to finance development activities planned under Outcome7: Modern setups and systems for scientific monitoring in Kunzila Watershed established and preliminary findings verified. The reason for the utilization of above the planned budget was that the 40% payment for ACACIA was above the planned budget when it also includes the 15% tax.

A total budget of € 259881 was allocated to finance development activities planned under Outcome 1: Watersheds are managed sustainably and ecosystem services enhance. The project utilized 101.1% of the allocated budget. The reason for excess was that developing nurseries demanded employment of additional daily laborers, which raised the expenditure a bit.

A total budget of € 291256 was allocated to finance development activities planned under Outcome3: Outcome 3: Improved capacities of institutions, community organizations, and groups for sustainable natural resource management and livelihoods. Many training and manual preparations/publications were not fully implemented during the budget year as time was against us and are pushed to the next year.

A total budget of € 452,943 was allocated to finance development activities planned under Outcome 2: Agricultural productivity and livelihoods enhanced. From this budget, 56.4% of the budget was utilized during the reporting period. The planned tractors and machinery for RUTH were not purchased due to a change in approach. In addition, there were delays in the implementation of homestead packages for many reasons such as the need for forage preparation, finalization of the credit system, etc.

A total fund of € 771,288.42 allocated to finance program costs, indirect costs such as office rent, headquarter staff, salaries of the project staff, etc. From this, the project utilized 76.1%. Delay in the employment of drivers (due to the delay in the purchases of vehicles), finding a reputable management consultant took a long time.

A total of € 936,542.53 was planned to finance the purchases of equipment, supplies, and other expenditures including travel-related expenses. Of this, 40% of the planned budget was utilized. The reasons are that equipment for the monitoring stations was not purchased due to the bureaucratic import system of the country. In addition, diverse inputs for FREG, and other demonstrations were not purchased due to the bureaucratic import system and the delay in some of the homestead activities, respectively. Furthermore, the planned equipment for RUTH was not purchased as we changed our approach.

title.narrative: Integrated water resource management

description.narrative: Integrated water resource management refers to outcomes that improve the recharge capacity of the landscape, proper management of wetlands, developing groundwater and surface water resources, protecting the quality of water and more importantly, reduced siltation of Lake Tana.

title.narrative: Degree of integrated water resource management implementation (1-10)

description.narrative: It is judged by taking the none existent baseline practice as 1 and what can be done at best as 10.

comment.narrative: A lot of activities are implemented to enhance groundwater recharge, reduce siltation into Lake Tana, and conserve water loss through IWM interventions. In addition, installation of hydrometric instruments, rainfall gauging stations, and groundwater monitoring stations contribute for scientific implementation of water resource interventions. Furthermore, water quality is made for Lake water, groundwater, rivers and springs. Finally, irrigation schemes (river diversion and surface water pump) and ponds are constructed to enhance economic use of water resources.

The degree of water resource management implementation (1-10) in the baseline situation was rated as 1 (very weak). The project targeted to raise this rating to 3. The project implemented several activities such as the construction of two community ponds, the construction of diverse soil and water conservation activities through community mobilizations, the construction of a diversion canal, and the like. Despite these efforts, the performances were limited especially in implementing conservation works that raise the rating from 1 only to 2.
When the project was extended for one more year due to the ongoing security problems, we simply take the previous year target of 8 as the targets for the current reporting period.
The plan was to reach rating of 8 but no major improvement was seen in the year due to the conflict thus, the rating remains the same as we reported last year, which was 7.

title.narrative: Hectars of forest(ed) land under sustainable managemnt or other improved practices

comment.narrative: New target was set when the project was extended for one more year due to the ongoing security problems. The targets that have not met over the original project period (March 2020 to December 2024, was set as the target for the extension period.

As indicated in Table 2 of the main narrative report, landscape restoration interventions encompass afforestation, closure of degraded lands, hillside rehabilitation, plantations on religious areas, wetlands, grazing lands, gullies, and homestead backyards. The total land area identified for restoration is 3,686 hectares, of which 499 hectares were considered restored at baseline. For the current budget year, the plan targeted significant progress; however, only 420 hectares (46% of the annual plan and about 11% of the cumulative restoration target) were achievedthrough area closure and plantations. The shortfall is primarily due to difficulties in securing collective action among land users, as the lack of coordinated decision-making has led to conflicting practices. This challenge was further intensified by the ongoing conflict, with the presence of opposing forces in the project area undermining accountability and consistent implementation. However the 46% performance levels may seem small, the achievement is very satisfactory given the current conflict situation in the areas.
The planned net increase in forested land of 601 ha during the year + 499 ha of baseline level would bring the cumulative target to 1100 ha.

Based on the baseline survey, the baseline forest(ed) land in the project area was 499 ha. The project planned to increase this area to 1100 in the implementation period of 2020-2021. Of, 146.5 ha of land is forested through diverse strategies such as treatment of gullies with the planting of forage trees, multipurpose trees, and grasses splits which amount to 40.5 ha of land. Similar interventions were also made through area closure of degraded lands and by planting different trees. Accordingly, 89 ha of land is closed from human and livestock contact. To ensure the sustainability of the area closure of degraded land and gully, 39 and 38 resource user associations are established for the gully and degraded lands that are closed. Furthermore, afforestation of communal lands and hillsides was also done on 17 ha of land. These interventions increased the previous 499 ha of forest land to 645.5 ha. Community mobilization and enforcement problems were the major reason for poor the performances
The net increase in forested land of 1190 ha in planning period + 1100 ha of previous year baseline would bring the total target of to 2290 ha.

Diverse interventions to increase forested lands are implemented during the year. Accordingly, 201 ha of land is newly developed. With the old 645.5 ha of forested lands it would have brought the performance to 846.5 ha. But there are also over exploitation of degraded lands and deforestation of existing one due to weak law enforcement by the respective institutions. This reduced the cumulative outcome to 821.5 ha.
The net increase in forested land of 510 ha in planning period + 2290 ha of previous year baseline would bring the total target to 2800 ha.

Forest lands are continuously squeezed and degraded lands, and communal lands that can be changed to forest lands are largely converted to farmlands and grazing lands. Efforts to protect the existing forests and develop new ones partly fail due to the weak enforcement of bylaws by the local institutions. A lot of efforts have been exerted by the project to coordinate collective actions, strengthen resource governance bodies, and enforce bylaws but these efforts have not brought the expected outcomes mainly due to the weak institutions.
The net increase in forested land of 510 ha in planning period + 2800 ha of previous year baseline would bring the total target to 3310 ha.

Forest lands are continuously squeezed and degraded lands, and communal lands that can be changed to forest lands are largely converted to farmlands and grazing lands. To curb this, the project exerted a lot of efforts to curb this trend. Accordingly, so far, a total of 82 ha of Church forests, 89 ha of communal forests, 79 ha of hillside and private plantations, 123 ha of gullies and riverine, 562 ha of degraded area closure, 55 ha of wetland, and 978 ha of homestead are covered with interventions that enrich the forest covers of the different land uses. Of these cumulative achievements, the forest coverage of 420.1 ha was improved in this budget year (2023-2024) which include 65 ha area closure, 25.5 gullies, 15.2 church forest, 15.4 wetland and 299 homestead lands) of the different lands . When the biological plantation of forage trees on farm lands are included, the figure will be much higher than the above. Yet, the performance is below the target. The reason was the planned interventions that improve forest covers of the different land uses was not implemented as planned due to the conflict in the project area and in the region at large.

title.narrative: Nutrition improvement

description.narrative: It refers to the number of hectares of farmland directly reached with activities to improve eco-efficiency. It includes all the soil and water conservation and lang management activities implemented through physical, biological and agroforestry measures. It specifically refers to the Integrated Watershed Management (IWM) implemented under Component 1 of the project sub-sectors.

title.narrative: Hectares of farmland directly reached with activities to improve eco-efficiency

comment.narrative: Based on the baseline study, areas of farmlands reached with improved eco-efficiency was 298 ha. In 2020-2021 project year, the project has reached an additional 617.8 ha of farmland with different activities that improve the eco-efficiency of the land. These interventions include construction of SWC works; planting of grass-strips; promotion of composts and treating acidic soils with lime. Furthermore, the promotion of fuel-saving stoves is also another eco-efficiency technology.

From Table 2 of the main report above, a restoration works of 552 ha of cultivated land was covered with grass strips, 299 ha of homestead development was implemented this year. In addition, the 25.5ha of gully closed and protected this year also improve the eco-efficiency of cultivated lands. Though the annual performance in terms of the original annual target was good, the performance in terms of the revised annual plan was so low. In an attempt to achieve full coverage of the different lands, there was a plan to cover 2713 ha of farmland, gully, and homestead lands with restoration works. Unfortunately, we were able to achieve only 876.5 (32.3% of the revised annual plan). The main reason was that the conflict situation doesn’t allow community mobilization and thus all the physical SWC works (mainly construction of bunds) that were planned to be implemented in 2024 on farmlands were not implemented at all. Thus, the focus was to cover low-slope cultivated lands with grass strips.

New target was set when the project was extended for one more year due to the ongoing security problems. The targets that have not met over the original project period (March 2020 to December 2024, was set as the target for the extension period.

From Table 2 of the main report, the project had set a total target of restoring 6,233 hectares of cultivated land. Out of this, 4,146 hectares were accomplished during the years 2021–2023. For the current year, the plan was to restore 2,084 hectares; however, only 484 hectares were achieved, representing 23% of the annual plan. The shortfall was mainly due to the conflict situation, which hindered community mobilization. The achievement obtained was made possible through a newly introduced implementationstrategy, whereby landowners were convinced to carry out restoration works on their own farms instead of the usual mass campaign approach. This strategy has shown promise and is planned to be continued in the coming year.

In retrospect, the target was found to be ambitious and exaggerated compared to the existing potential. But the performance was also somehow not as expected to be for many reasons. One of the major problem was the political unrest and peace situations in the region that undermined the efforts to organize and coordinate collective actions to construct and maintain physical SWC practices, protect and sustain area exclusions, gully treatments, grazing land rehabilitations, etc.

title.narrative: Number of smallscale producers directly reached with activities to increase productivity/income

comment.narrative: A large number of households participated in the various livelihood and agricultural productivity enhancement interventions such as dairy, fattening (cattle and shoat), poultry, apiculture, sheep rearing, sheep breed improvements, horticulture production (vegetable and fruits) using rainfed and irrigation, high-yielding crop varieties, agricultural mechanizations, etc. The project also introduced a well-designed and innovative financial service strengthening fund through SACCOs which dramatically increased the access of farmers to saving and credit services. The revolving fund injected into the SACCOs not only increased the amounts of loans by 310%, savings by 210%, and the dividend they earn from the profit by 573%.

From Table 3 & 4 above, HHs that increased their income in 2024 are 1097 from veg, 748 HHs from Ox fattening and 819 from other livestock productions that bring a total of 2664. This number is exaggerated because double counting among years and overlapping of commodities. Therefore, the net data should be collected for finalize this report.

New target was set when the project was extended for one more year due to the ongoing security problems. The targets that have not met over the original project period (March 2020 to December 2024, was set as the target for the extension period.

Since the inception of the project in 2020, the objective has been to improve the livelihoods of about 75% of the project community by increasing the production and productivity of various commodities such as fruits and vegetables, livestock, and post-harvest technologies. To date, including the current year, the project has reached 4,731 households, both homestead andnon-homestead. However, considerable effort is still required to engage households in multiple intervention packages to ensure that their incomes increase as intended.(See livelihood Table in the published narrative report)

The project planned to reach 784 small-scale producers with activities to increase productivity/income. The project designed diverse interventions to reach the smallscale producers by promoting productivity/income raising technologies on production of vegetables, fruits, cash crops (gesho, coffee), livestock production (fattening, poultry, beekeeping, sheep breeding, dairy, etc.), field crops (improved variety, introduction of new crop - upland rice, fertility management), and by enabling you to acquire special skills demanded by the market, etc. In the project year, 609 smallscale producers are reached with one or more of the above technologies. Access to credit service was the main reason for low performance. The project is working to address this problem through the Saving and Credit Cooperatives operating in the areas.

title.narrative: Nutrition improvement

description.narrative: Nutrition improvement is one of the core aim of the project. It includes the change in dietary habit of the households, feeding tradition of especially children, increased diversity of diets, enhanced production and consumption of nutritionally valuable diets especially fruits and vegetables.

title.narrative: Number of people directly reached with activiteis to improve nutrition

comment.narrative: Originally, the baseline was wrongly reported as 495 by taking the number households instead of the number of people which was 2763

New target was set when the project was extended for one more year due to the ongoing security problems. The targets that have not met over the original project period (March 2020 to December 2024, was set as the target for the extension period.

At the start of the project, it was estimated that about 495 people were relatively nutrition-secure, while an additional 5,545 people were targeted over the five years to improve their nutritional status through interventions such as fruits, vegetables, and livestock products, including poultry, apiculture, and dairy. To date, including the current year, about 2,979 households have reported relative improvements in nutrition (see Annex Table 6.3), based on the resources they possess. This represents approximately 54% of the five-year target, indicating significant progress, though continued efforts are required to fully achieve the intended outcomes. Encouragingly, communities are increasingly utilizing their own products for household consumption in addition to marketing.
The target was originally expressed in terms of households (2079 households) and corrected into 11227 number of people.

Concerted efforts were made to improve household nutrition through demonstration of food preparation, teaching to change dietary habits, implement the production and consumption of vegetable and fruit productions, introduce new nutritionally valuable fruit such as water melon, implement the production, productivity and consumption of poultry and dairy production. Good results are achieved in introducing improved vegetable and fruit crops and improved dairy breeds, expand the production and consumption of these products. But several nutrition enhancement interventions are at their early stage (fruits not ready for harvest), In addition, the implementation of poultry production was jeopardized by the ban on the movement of chicken by the government due to the outbreak of Newcastle, and coccidiosis diseases. Furthermore, many of the vegetable varieties and types are new to the area and farmers are just starting.

Since fruits stay few years, we only considered vegetables and livestock products to calculate the nutrition improvements. In this regard, the communities are developing utilization of their products in addition to marketing. In 2024: 1097 HHs from veg, 819 HHs from livestock except ox fattening as all are for sale

The project encourages the households that participated in the various types of livelihood interventions to consume at least 30 percent of the output they produced through the livelihood interventions. In addition, the project involved the husbands and wives of a large number of households in the food preparation and tasting event organized by the project. Moreover, the project uses 59 Gender Model Family groups organized by the project to promote household nutrition.
Like the baseline, 1386 number of households of was wrongly taken in determining the target instead of the number of people which was equal to 7484 people.

To improve the nutritional status of households, the project implemented various interventions by implementing integrated homestead packages that are implemented in the backyard of households. The homestead package is a bundle of technologies consisting of vegetable production, fruit production, poultry production, beekeeping, dairy production, sheep/goat production etc. The aim is to encourage farmers to use portions of these products for household consumption. Demonstrating improved food preparation is also part of the intervention. A total of 439 households was reported as actual performance which in terms of number of people was equal to 2371.

comment.narrative: A number of activities that benefit many farmers were planned to be implemented through community mobilization. Almost no community mobilization works have been performed elsewhere in the region due to the existing political conflict and security problems. But the project was able to mobilize communities to implement some activities such as SWC works, gully treatment, area exclusion, etc. Though the performance vis-a-vis the plan is not good, it was a great success compared to other areas. The project implemented diverse activities that benefited 672 farmers.

Participation of local communities was very good as manifested by their participation in managing small-scale irrigation schemes and community ponds, contributing their labor and contributing money to hire guards and engine operator

Practical implementation of project activities were delayed due other competing priorities of local government that weakened their support for project activities (political conflict and peace problems in the region). Extremely high inflation and supply shocks of construction materials have delayed the construction of irrigation schemes.

New target was set when the project was extended for one more year due to the ongoing security problems. The targets that have not met over the original project period (March 2020 to December 2024, was set as the target for the extension period.

The planned construction of a new irrigation scheme at Sanketa village, designed to cover 320 hectares and benefit about 1,000 households, as well as the construction of 10 new community ponds expected to benefit more than 500 people, could not be implemented due to the conflict situation in the region. However, some progress was achieved through small-scale water harvesting technologies. Specifically, 14 households adopted roof water harvesting, 50 households upgraded manual wells, and 120 households benefited from simple pulley technologies. In total, this accounts for 184 households, or approximately 920 people (assuming an average family size of 5), who accessed improved water sources (see Table 5). Overall, the poor performance in planned irrigation and water harvesting interventions was mainly attributed to security challenges.

The planned construction of new irrigation schemes, Ponds, SS dams were not implemented mainly due to the conflict problem in the region. Furthermore, as indicated in the description of the current conflict, the surface pump irrigation scheme that was under construction of at Ambesswork village Estumit kebele which could have been functional and benefited more than 600 people was destroyed by a mob. The 320 new beneficiaries reported here was due to the irrigation extension work on the reservoir at Mehalgie 44 HHs and different water technologies for 12 HHs, a total of 56 HHs or 320 people (5.5 family size) have been used (see Table 5). Generally, the poor performance was mainly due to the security challenge.
